name: Question 2
worked_solution:
First, we substitute $u=\sqrt{x}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,⟹\,2\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $x\to \infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=\sqrt{x}$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $1$ | $\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(u)]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)] \\  & =2\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)]-\frac{\pi }{4})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x),$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)]=-\frac{\pi }{2}$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)]=\frac{\pi }{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14052212/assets/46e6cf2950c99831a7445a862fb36a6a7b8f9233a82e49c7cf5da4a383ec4756.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}(x+1)}\,\text{d}x & =2\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(a)]-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we substitute u=x. Differentiating, we get dudx=12x⟹2du=1xdx.

Since u→∞ when x→∞, the table for the limits of integration using the rule u=x is as follows:

x 1 ∞
u 1 ∞

So, the integral in terms of the new variable u is

∫1∞1x(x+1)dx=2∫1∞1u2+1du.

Now, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter a, integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as a→∞.

∫1∞1x(x+1)dx=2∫1∞1u2+1du=2⋅lima→∞∫1a1u2+1dx=2⋅lima→∞[arctan⁡(u)]1a=2⋅lima→∞[arctan⁡(a)−arctan⁡(1)]=2⋅(lima→∞[arctan⁡(a)]−π4)

Finally, recall the end behavior of the function y=arctan⁡(x), shown in the graph below:

  • limx→−∞[arctan⁡(x)]=−π2

  • limx→∞[arctan⁡(x)]=π2

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

∫1∞1x(x+1)dx=2⋅(lima→∞[arctan⁡(a)]−π4)=2⋅(π2−π4)=2⋅π4=π2.
